correctness.rationale: For an interior target the second phase rho restricts the ordinate to (rho-ax)/(b*pi); exactly the phases in (0,b*pi] persist at small positive x, including the upper endpoint from inside the rectangle. Substitution gives the stated quadratic and two distinct first-phase roots per large integer band; the Jacobian is nonzero and has magnitude 4ab(1+pi^2/x^2) times sqrt(u(1-u)v(1-v)). Summing its reciprocals gives a finite weight with the stated first-order term and O(delta^2) error. Outside null critical curves ordinary local change of variables gives the density, the proposed limit has mass one, and Scheffe gives total variation. Complete monotone half-periods have one inverse per interior level; a nonempty incomplete half-period adds one on a proper interval, proving the iff.
